description: QUASIX is a team passionate about space, science, and technology. We aim to turn creative ideas into innovative solutions using NASA's open data. We're looking for enthusiastic members interested in AI/ML, programming, data science, design, astronomy, and research. We value creativity, teamwork, and curiosity. Join QUASIX to solve challenges, build impactful projects, and explore the universe together! 🚀
summary:
QUASIX is a browser based 3D space mission design game that was made for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. People take on the job of aerospace engineers to create send and manage a 3U CubeSat from the start.
To solve the Space Mission Design Game challenge QUASIX turns real world systems engineering into a game. Players choose frames, power systems, sensors and communication equipment while making sure to meet important limits like weight, power use, cost, launch vehicles and the places where the satellite will orbit. The game has five Earth-observation campaigns cyclones, wildfires, Arctic sea ice, volcanic activity and coral bleaching. It uses NASA data getting up-to-date natural-event data from NASA EONET and local weather information from NASA POWER. Players then see their satellites path. Do a staged flight simulation with live data and a score that shows how much science they can gather.

Spacecraft engineering can seem hard for most people because of the high technical level needed. By turning aerospace choices into a hands-on trial and error web experience built with React and Three.js QUASIX brings space science within reach. It inspires interest. Teaches systems-engineering thinking to learners all, around the world.
details:
# QUASIX – Interactive 3D Space Mission Design Game

QUASIX is a 3D space mission design game created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 specifically for the Space Mission Design Game challenge.

The project wants to make spacecraft engineering and earth observation missions easier to learn by using a fun browser-based simulation. Players become mission designers. Build a 3U CubeSat by choosing structural parts, power systems, scientific instruments and communication gear.

QUASIX shows engineering trade offs such as spacecraft mass, power use, component costs, launch vehicle choice and orbital regimes. Players move through steps: campaign selection, spacecraft assembly launch prep orbit view, target choice and flight simulation.

QUASIX offers five earth observation campaigns that cover cyclones, wildfires, arctic sea ice, volcanic activity and coral bleaching. NASA EONET is built in to get natural event data and NASA POWER supplies weather data such as temperature, wind and rain, for chosen target spots.

The flight simulation shows staged mission steps, telemetry readouts, science yield calculations and mission results. Whether a configuration succeeds or fails QUASIX gives feedback that pushes players to grasp engineering limits and rebuild their spacecraft.

The app was built with React, Vite, JavaScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, React Three Drei, Leaflet and Lucide React.

Our goal is to turn aerospace ideas into an interactive learning tool that sparks experimentation, scientific curiosity and systems engineering thinking.
